messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: AUTH_VERIFY_ERRORS_HIGH for service=auth-service in prod-us-west :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident triggered — Priority: P1. Responders: sarah (oncall), mike (eng-sre).

sarah (oncall): I'm on it, acked from phone. Collecting initial scope. Anyone seeing customer reports?

carol (customer-ops): getting ticket spam from enterprise customers in US-WEST complaining about 401s when calling Redwood API with current tokens. Severity: multiple customers.

mike (eng-sre): seeing spike in auth verify failures in prod-us-west and prod-eu-west. 401 rate ~18% of requests for /v1/auth/verify in the last 5m. Error log: "signature verification failed: kid not found in JWKS".

jin (auth): that sounds like a JWKS / key-id mismatch — probably a key rotation went partially through. I just checked key-propagation logs, there was a rotation job 23:02Z that finished but some caches still had old keys.

sarah (oncall): can you post the rotation job id and which KMS was used? We need to know if we can roll back quickly.

jin (auth): rotation-id rot-2026-03-14-23-02, KMS: aws-kms-prod, manager: key-manager-v2. The rotation succeeded in control plane but the auth-runtime pods read JWKS from the central cache which had a TTL of 300s; however CDN edge caches also pulled the new JWKS and some verifiers now can't find the old kid. Mixed population.

eve (eng-runtime): Confirmed mixed verifiers. Some verifier instances got new keys and dropped the old kid entry, others still expect old. So tokens signed with old kid fail on the new verifiers.

mike (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) re-publish old key into JWKS (fast) 2) roll back rotation in KMS (riskier) 3) enable verifier fallback to cached key store for legacy kid (requires deploy). Suggest re-publish old key to JWKS and set longer propagation flag while we stabilize.

jin (auth): I can republish the old key to JWKS and pin it for 30 minutes. Doing it now. Will also lower TTL on edge caches to 60s.

incident-bot: Action started: auth-team republish-key rot-2026-03-14-23-02 -> underway.

carol (customer-ops): i'll notify impacted customers that we're investigating and have a mitigation in progress. Notifying top 5 affected customers with ETA 15m.

jin (auth): republish completed. JWKS now contains both keys; control-plane flagged as legacy-retain=true for 30m. Edge TTL update issued.

mike (eng-sre): monitoring: 401 rate dropping from 18% -> 3% over the last 6m. Latency unchanged. Looks like the republish worked.

sarah (oncall): good. Can we confirm no data leakage risk? Why were both keys removed from some verifiers? We need RCA items.

jin (auth): preliminary theory: rotation job incorrectly set a purge flag (purge_old_keys=true) downstream in cache invalidation step. Control plane rotation marked success but cache invalidation propagated before legacy re-publish. I'll collect logs.

incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty alert resolved (AUTH_VERIFY_ERRORS_HIGH) by sarah (oncall).

carol (customer-ops): Customer update: first wave of emails sent. Most customers report restored access. One customer (acme-corp) had longer issues due to client side caching of JWT public keys. Advising them to clear JWKS cache or restart clients.

mike (eng-sre): quant: approx 42M auth verify attempts in the 30m window; 7.6M failed at peak. Affected regions: us-west ~70%, eu-west ~20%, ap-south ~10% (due to cross-region token verifications).

jin (auth): action items I'm kicking off: 1) roll forward fix to rotation job to remove purge_old_keys (PR drafted) 2) add safety: publish both keys before changing cache pointers 3) add QA regression for partial-propagation scenarios 4) run backfill to ensure no stale caches remain.

carol (customer-ops): follow-up: create a customer incident doc and coordinate credits/SLAs for affected tenants.

mike (eng-sre): i'm going to keep an eye on metrics for 1h. Reopening if 401s >1% sustained.

oncall-handoff-bot: Handoff planned: sarah (oncall) -> mike (eng-sre) at 02:00Z. Please include summary and outstanding tasks.

sarah (oncall): handing off now. Summary: rotation caused JWKS kid mismatch, republished old key, impact reduced to ~3% then sub-1%. Outstanding: PR to rotation job, add tests, verify cache purge behavior, prepare postmortem and customer comms.

mike (eng-sre): ack and taking over monitoring. I'll coordinate postmortem template and file action items.

jin (auth): adding one more: audit KMS logs for rotation command origin to ensure no accidental repeats.

carol (customer-ops): drafting the customer incident timeline doc, will attach to the postmortem.

incident-bot: This thread will be archived after 72h. For follow-ups, add tags: postmortem, auth, jwks, rotation.

sarah (oncall): thanks team. Good recovery. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-sre): filing postmortem now and assigning actions to owner list.

jin (auth): will PR and tests today.

carol (customer-ops): will follow up on credits and customer comms.

mike (eng-sre): last check at handoff: 401 rate 0.7% in last 5m, trending down. Closing active incident.
